brief: Tonight is Legs B, and every number on your card is exactly the same as the one you saw yesterday. That is on purpose. Nothing new has been logged since your pull session on 15 September, so there is no new information to change a single weight, and a trainer who moves your numbers without new evidence is just guessing twice. Here is what I can tell about yesterday: there is no session in the app for 16 September, and each of your last five workouts landed in the app the same evening, within half an hour of your final set. So it reads like you took yesterday off. I am not certain of that, and I am not going to pretend I am. If it turns out you did train and it syncs later, this whole packet steps aside and the app goes back to its own standing rules. Tonight: the RDL is still a deliberate back-off at three sets, 135 then 155 twice, instead of four sets up to 180. Your 180 for 10 is banked and safe. I am holding 190 back not because of a day count but because your deadlift went backwards between 28 August and 10 September, from 265 for 5 twice down to 255 for 4 twice, and because nobody has weighed you in 25 days, so there is no way to read whether you are recovering. The deload starts on 21 September and 190 is waiting for you on the other side of it. Everything else stands as before: leg press 130, 150, 170; leg curl opens at 110 and keeps its 145 top set; hip abductor two sets at 110; hip adductor 105 twice with 15 reps the target; calf press 240, 260, 260 and the job is 15 on all three; cable crunch 65 for three sets of 12; hanging leg raise two sets, stop each one when your form goes rather than at a count. One correction I owe you from yesterday's card, below. And one thing outside the gym: get on a scale this week. The last bodyweight in the app is 207 lb from 23 August.

flags.note: Nothing was logged for yesterday, 16 September. Your last five sessions each landed in the app the same evening within half an hour of the last set, so it reads as a rest day, but I cannot prove it. If you did train and it syncs later, tonight's numbers step aside and the app uses its standing rules.

Correction to yesterday's card: it told you your program trainer had put a card on the Smith RDL name explaining why it is staying. There was no such card. The truth is that the slot is still called Smith RDL, you are doing it with a barbell, and there is no question in front of you about it right now — an earlier ask to rename it went unanswered from 6 to 11 September and your program trainer chose not to re-file it today rather than nag you.

Your recovery trainer kept its veto on adding weight to the RDL, and I upheld it. It dropped the 'fourth day in a row' argument once yesterday came up empty, and rested the veto on the two facts that did not change: your deadlift lost reps between 28 August and 10 September, and there is no bodyweight reading to tell recovery from grinding.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August — 207 lb, 25 days ago. With the show on 1 March this is the one number nobody can estimate for you.

Five lifts run on both leg days — leg curl, both hip machines, calf press and cable crunch — and each day is progressing off its own history, so the same muscle carries two different working weights. Nobody has decided whether Legs A is meant to be the lighter day. This is still open, it is about weights rather than program structure so it cannot become a Yes/No card, and it needs you and me in a session.
Meso 2, week 4 of 4 — the last hard week. The deload starts 21 September. Three trainers reported, six disagreements settled, one tiredness veto upheld, and no pain or injury objection was raised.

Two of your trainers changed their own minds overnight and both moved toward the same thing: your hip abductor and hanging leg raise numbers from 5 September were typed into your phone from memory, not recorded as you lifted, so neither lift gets a raise built on them. They now agree on the hanging leg raise, which they did not yesterday.

proposals.why: The hanging leg raise is the only thing left that makes Legs B different from Legs A, but it sits dead last on a twenty-two set night, and on 5 September both its sets were typed one second apart the following day — this runs it ahead of the cable crunch instead of leaving it at the tail.

Both push days now press dumbbells overhead at 8 to 10 reps, and Push B does it first and heaviest, so this takes the Push A sets to 10 to 12 and lets the two days stop being the same session — the same way your chest press already splits 10 to 12 on Push A and 8 to 10 on Push B.

dissent.progression: Both heavy sets hit 180 for 10, the top of the range, logged minutes apart, so the step to 190 is earned.
dissent.recovery: Three sets, stop at 155 — the deadlift already lost reps last week and there is no bodyweight reading to tell recovery from grinding.
dissent.why: I nearly overturned this today. Yesterday's ruling leaned partly on it being his fourth straight training day, and that argument is gone: nothing was logged for 16 September and his last five sessions all synced the same evening, so he most likely rested. But the recovery seat dropped that argument itself and rested its veto on the two facts that did not move — the deadlift going from 265 for 5 twice on 28 August to 255 for 4 twice on 10 September, and 25 days with no bodyweight. A probable rest day is an inference I drew from sync timestamps, not a logged fact, and it is not strong enough to put 190 lb on the heavy hinge in the last week of a build block when the deload is four days out and 190 costs him nothing to wait for. Changing his card overnight with no new logged data is also exactly how this program produced four different ramps from one body of evidence. Numbers hold.

dissent.progression: All three sets finished at 12, the top of the range, with real minutes between them, so each goes up one 10 lb step.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 120, 140 and 160 — he pressed legs on 13 September and this is the last week of a build block.
dissent.why: Same ruling as yesterday, and the reasoning is unchanged because the evidence is unchanged. This is measured work, all three sets finished at the top of the range, the step is the standard 10 lb, and it is a machine press with nowhere to get hurt. I have already taken the load off the hinge that opens the night, so the session as a whole is still lighter than last time with this raise in it.

dissent.progression: Hold 145 until it gives 12, and move the opening set from 100 to 110.
dissent.recovery: Two sets at 130 — hamstrings again within five days and the RDL comes first tonight.
dissent.why: Same ruling as yesterday. Recovery's case is that the RDL will have taxed the hamstrings first, and I have cut the RDL to 155 for three sets, which removes most of that. Nothing here adds weight to the top set; the only thing that moves is the warm-up, and 130 for 12 twice on 13 September proves 110 is not a hard opener.

dissent.progression: The 135 top set was never measured, so open at 127.5 and earn 135 tonight.
dissent.recovery: Stay at 110 — the only measured reading on this machine is 110 for 12 on 13 September.
dissent.why: The progression seat corrected itself here overnight, unprompted: it had been asking for 145 off a 5 September set that was typed in 0.8 seconds after the one before it, and it now agrees that set was recalled rather than lifted. That is real and it deserves credit. But it still wants to open at 127.5, which comes from the same untrustworthy session, and his last honest reading on this machine is 110 for 12 four days ago. I am not jumping him from 110 to 127.5 on a session whose numbers we have just agreed were written from memory. Tonight at 110 gives us one clean reading to build on, and it is the same number his card already showed him yesterday.

dissent.progression: Same weights as last time — 260 is not finished until all three sets give 15.
dissent.recovery: Stay at 240 rather than chasing 260 in the last week of a build block.
dissent.why: Same ruling as yesterday. Nothing goes up either way, so the only question is whether to go backwards, and he already did 260 for 15 on a measured set on 5 September. Dropping to 240 would take away work he has proven. Calves are also the least fatiguing thing on tonight's card.

dissent.progression: Same 65 for three sets, and 12 reps is what earns more weight.
dissent.recovery: Same 65, but two sets is enough with abs already worked this week.
dissent.why: Same ruling as yesterday. The weight is not in dispute, only the third set. Abs are the cheapest sets in the session and the slot asks for three. If a fatigue problem shows up tonight, it will not be in a cable crunch.

overrides.reason: Same as yesterday — nothing new was logged, so nothing moves. This is a deliberate back-off: three sets topping at 155 instead of 180, because your deadlift lost reps between 28 August and 10 September and nobody has weighed you in 25 days. Your 180 for 10 is banked and 190 is the target after the deload.
All three sets finished at 12 last time, the top of the range, so each one goes up one 10 lb step. Start at 10 reps and work back up to 12.

145 only gave 10 reps last time, so the top set stays where it is until it gives 12. The one change is the opening set: you did 130 for 12 twice on 13 September, so 100 is too light and it opens at 110.

The heavier 5 September numbers were typed into your phone 0.8 seconds apart, so they were recalled rather than measured and both your trainers now agree we should not build on them. Your last real reading is 110 for 12 on 13 September — tonight is 110 for two sets, and what you log becomes the number we use.
Both trainers agree here: 105 on 5 September for 12 and 105 again on 13 September for 13. The weight stays and the job tonight is 15 on both sets.
Nothing goes up. You got 260 for 15 once on 5 September and then dropped to 13 on the last set, so 260 is not finished — same three weights, and the job is 15 on all three.
65 for 10 on 5 September and 65 for 11 on 13 September — the reps are climbing but 12 is the number that earns more weight. Hold 65 and get 12 on all three sets.

Both trainers now agree on this one. Last time's two sets of 12 were typed in the next day, one second apart, so there is no real reading to add a rep to. Repeat two bodyweight sets and stop each one when your form goes, not at a count.
